annotation.title_en: The Secret of the Red Apple
annotation.summary_en: A father and son eavesdrop on a conversation between the new bride and mother-in-law, only to discover shocking secrets about their pasts.
annotation.summary_detailed_en: The sketch opens in a family apartment where a father and son are discussing the wedding night. The father reminisces about his own wedding twenty-five years ago and how the neighbors complained about the noise. The son is anxious about his new bride, but the father reassures him. The bride and the mother-in-law (both played by male comedians in drag) retreat to a side room to have a heart-to-heart conversation as the 'holy women of the hearth.' Suspicious, the father and son sneak to the door to eavesdrop. Inside, the bride confesses she has a secret: she tells the mother-in-law not to bother bringing the traditional 'red apple' to her parents' house. She explains her colorful past, mentioning she lived in a dormitory and has 'experience' with men, before finally bluntly stating, 'I am a man.' The mother-in-law, instead of being horrified by the gender reveal, is relieved because she thought it was 'something bad.' She then reveals her own secret: that she was actually a virgin when she married the 'idiot' father. Overhearing this, the father is devastated, calling them both 'immoral,' and the sketch ends with him distraught at the doorway.
